entities.summary: Eric Allen Johnston was a business owner, president of the United States Chamber of Commerce, a Republican Party activist, president of the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA), and a U.S. government special projects administrator and envoy for both Democratic and Republican administrations. As president of the MPAA, he abbreviated the organization's name, convened the closed-door meeting of motion picture company executives at New York City's Waldorf-Astoria Hotel that led to Waldorf Statement in 1947 and the Hollywood blacklist, and discreetly liberalized the Motion Picture Production Code.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As president of the MPAA, Johnston's actions led to the Hollywood blacklist, which resulted in the blacklisting of over 500 individuals and the exile of many artists from the film industry for perceived leftist or communist sympathies. His liberalization of the Motion Picture Production Code also had a lasting impact on the film industry.
